posts.title: The Legend of St. Disco Ball (And the Practice of Radical Amazement)
posts.description: Fifty-five years ago, I was a two-year-old kid living on an Air Force base in Bitburg, Germany. My memories of that time are a bit fuzzy, much like looking through a frosted window, but one feeling remains crystal clear: the nervous, heart-pounding anticipation of December. Me wandering and wondering in Germany circa 1971 Before Christmas, we washed and cleaned our little black winter boots and left them outside our door, waiting for St. Nicholas to visit. I can still remember the glorious anxiety of knowing he was making his way through the frosty town, street by street, until he finally reached our door to leave his wonderful surprises. To a child, it was pure, unadulterated magic. As writers, we spend a lot of time trying to bottle that exact feeling. We dig into our pasts, searching for the frequency of childhood wonder so we can broadcast it onto the page. But lately, I’ve realized we do not just have to mine our memories for magic. posts.title: Writing While the World Burns: Thoughts from Sabyasachi Roy. ~Christy Mihaly
posts.description: That Burning World Lately, it's been hard for me to get any writing done. Among other distractions, I have an aging parent who needs an increasing amount of my time and care. There's endless perpetual misery on my newsfeed. Oh, and book bans, funding cuts, and manuscript rejections. It gets heavy. I'm writing this on Election Day. When it's posted, we’ll be confronting all manner of crises and distractions competing for our attention -- this week and going forward. So, why write? Or, how can we? Writing While the World Burns This title caught my eye: Writing While the World Burns, by Sabyasachi Roy . I finished it in one sitting. Below, I’ll share where I found it, because it’s a resource I recommend. But first, a bit about Roy's words. In the introduction, he captures how I’ve been feeling: Somewhere, rent just went up again. Groceries cost more than last week. A job offer fell through. A visa was denied. A border closed. posts.title: STEAMWORKS wth Jen Malia and JUNE'S SOLAR OVEN & Craft Chat with Jen & Kathy Halsey
posts.description: June’s Solar Oven Book Review I was lucky to meet Jen Malia at the 2023 NCTE National Convention In Columbus, Ohio, and have been reading her chapter books and following her career ever since. JUNE’S SOLAR OVEN , a STEAM picture book, features June and her science club who are exploring solar, energy, and engineering through trial and error. However, the science club has moved locations to a local park and June feels uncomfortable in new places. Yet, neurodivergent June wants to show up for her friends, and science is her superpower. After some encouragement from her big sister and with her trusty headphones that help her deal with sensory issues, June is ready to join Eli and Sofia, her partners, with five other teams to find the best method to layer pepperoni and cheese and create the most delicious pizza cracker. Science teachers, librarians, and homeschooled students will appreciate the backmatter replete with a short glossary of science terms, simple directions to experiment with
